claims.text: The baseline alloy is as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
Partial replacement of Hf by additional Zr should be tested in HfMoTaTiZr.
Increasing the Zr fraction at the expense of Hf will decrease alloy density because Zr has a lower atomic mass than Hf.
The modified alloy will retain a single-phase BCC solid solution.
The modified alloy will retain lattice distortion and grain structure similar to those of the baseline.
Hf-to-Zr substitution will preserve solid-solution strengthening.
Edge- and screw-dislocation-mediated deformation mechanisms are responsible for the alloy's high room- and elevated-temperature yield strengths.
The Hf-to-Zr modification is expected to reduce density by approximately 10–15%.
The modified alloy's room-temperature yield strength will remain within 10% of 1600 MPa.
The modified alloy's yield strength at 1000 °C will remain within 10% of 855 MPa.
The modified alloy will preserve the baseline alloy's ductility.
The cited study fabricated and examined as-cast HfMoTaTiZr and related refractory alloys and considered elemental effects, phase formation, and solution strengthening.
Excessive Hf-to-Zr substitution may weaken elevated-temperature performance or alter deformation mechanisms.
The baseline and modified alloys will be compared after identical casting and homogenization treatments using density, room-temperature tensile, and 1000 °C tensile measurements.
The hypothesis is rejected if density decreases by less than 10% or either room-temperature or 1000 °C yield strength differs from baseline by more than 10%.

contradictions.description: Preserved ductility is part of the predicted performance and ductility is measured, but the rejection rule applies quantitative limits only to density and yield strengths. Thus, complete loss of ductility would not explicitly falsify the stated hypothesis.
